facts.claim: Lilongwe is named after the river that runs through the city and has been an administrative centre since 1904.

source.quote: Lilongwe, named after the river that runs through the city

facts.claim: Its importance as an agricultural market centre grew in the 1920s, linked to a tobacco industry in its hinterland and its position at a road junction.

source.publisher: African Cities Research Consortium (ICLEI Africa, ODI)

facts.claim: Malawi became independent in 1964 with Hastings Banda as first prime minister.

source.title: Hastings Kamuzu Banda (Research Starter)
source.author: David Barratt
source.quote: Self-government followed in 1962 and full independence in 1964.

facts.claim: The government decided in 1965 to move the capital from Zomba to Lilongwe, one year after independence, but the move was not completed until 1975.

source.title: Lilongwe: City report (Working Paper 13)
source.author: Donald Brown, Mtafu Manda, Tuntu Mwalyambwile
source.quote: While the decision to relocate the capital was made in 1965, it was not relocated until 1975.

facts.claim: Construction of Capital Hill, the site of central government, began in 1969; the first master plan (1968) was prepared with South African planners and envisaged a garden city.

places.name: Lilongwe Wildlife Centre
places.what: A wildlife rescue and rehabilitation sanctuary run by the Lilongwe Wildlife Trust inside a nature reserve in the middle of the capital. It cares for injured and orphaned animals.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: In the centre of the capital

source.title: Lilongwe Wildlife Centre recognised again with prestigious accreditation
source.quote: Located in the centre of Malawi’s capital city.

source.title: Lilongwe Wildlife Centre recognised again with prestigious accreditation
source.quote: which was set up in 2007.

source.title: Protecting the wild heart of the city and beyond
source.author: Kate Moore, Lilongwe Wildlife Trust
source.quote: the 200-ha nature reserve right in the heart of the city remains intact.

facts.label: Role
facts.value: Only wildlife rehabilitation sanctuary in Malawi and largest environmental education centre

source.title: Protecting the wild heart of the city and beyond

places.name: Malawi Parliament Building (Capital Hill)
places.what: The seat of Malawi's National Assembly, on the government district planned from 1969. Its dome is the largest in Malawi.

source.publisher: African State Architecture (SOAS University of London)
source.quote: The building was opened in 2010 and serves as the physical symbol of Malawi's representative political institution.

places.name: Kamuzu Mausoleum
places.what: The tomb of Malawi's first president, Hastings Kamuzu Banda, in Lilongwe. It was built in the 2000s as a two-storey marble-and-granite structure.

places.name: Lilongwe open markets (the Lilongwe market)
places.what: Lilongwe's open markets are the main food source for most residents. The council reports 41 designated markets, the largest being 'the Lilongwe market'.

source.title: Informal Economy Budget Analysis for Lilongwe City in Malawi (WIEGO Resource Document 13)
source.author: Sera Rose Gondwe, Debbie Budlender
source.quote: Lilongwe City Council reported a total of 41 open markets that accommodated 14,468 traders.

facts.label: Reliance
facts.value: Over 80 percent of residents use open markets for food

source.title: Informal Economy Budget Analysis for Lilongwe City in Malawi (WIEGO Resource Document 13)
source.author: Sera Rose Gondwe, Debbie Budlender
source.quote: over 80 per cent of residents rely on open markets as a food source
